claims.subject: Whether our agents can send email
claims.means: Drafting and sending are different permissions. Sending is denied at the configuration layer, so it is not a policy an agent can be talked out of.

claims.subject: Whether our agents can reach a shell
claims.means: The load-bearing one. An agent that can reach a shell can step around every other control here, so it is denied outright.

claims.subject: Deny rules that have survived a live attack
claims.means: A rule nobody has attacked is a claim, not a control. This counts only the ones something has actually tried to break. The rest are listed as untested, on purpose.
claims.text: — deny rules have survived a live attack.
claims.missing: none of the 4 deny rules has been attacked yet — the canary-injection drill is defined but has never been armed, so there is no survival to report

claims.subject: Automated checks on what this system may state
claims.means: The same discipline this page runs on. If any of them fail, the number here is withheld rather than rounded.
claims.detail: assertions that stop the OS stating what its inputs do not support
claims.text: 221 automated checks stop this system from stating what it cannot prove.

claims.subject: Facts re-checked across every surface
claims.means: A number changed in one place and left stale everywhere else is the most common way a company starts lying by accident. A machine checks, not a person.
claims.text: 43 facts are re-checked across every surface each week.

claims.subject: Scheduled jobs running with no human present
claims.means: Not a demo. This is the system we sell, running the business that sells it.
claims.detail: scheduled jobs that run with no human present
claims.text: 30 scheduled jobs run this company with no human present.

claims.subject: Last diff of what runs against what is sanctioned
claims.means: A weekly diff of what is actually running against what is approved to run. Unapproved automation is how an AI system quietly becomes something nobody chose.
claims.detail: last diff of what is running against what is sanctioned
claims.text: Last checked 2026-08-13: everything running is on the sanctioned list.

claims.subject: Last fault injected on purpose
claims.means: We break it on purpose, on a schedule, and record whether we noticed. A control with no drill behind it is not evidence of anything.

rows.means: The agents cannot run shell commands. This is the load-bearing one: an agent that can shell can bypass every other control on this page.
The agents cannot send email. They draft; a human sends.

controls.activeFileNote: The ACTIVE gate is the runtime host's own ~/.claude/settings.json. This page read the repo's reference copy — they are kept in sync by hand, so a drift between them is possible and is not detected here.

contract: Every claim on the site is bound to a check that runs. Past its ttlDays the value is withheld and what is missing is named in its place. Nothing here falls back to a cached number.
boundTo: Reliability and process only. Volume claims — clients, revenue, hours saved — are refused at generation time, not by review.
